text: "Doki Doki Morning" is a song by the Japanese heavy metal band Babymetal, released in Japan as an independent DVD single on October 22, 2011, and serves as the first single from their debut album Babymetal. The song introduced all three members to heavy metal music; Nakamoto noted she had never heard such musical heaviness before, while Mizuno initially preferred dancing over singing. During production, the signature Kitsune hand gesture (similar to the sign of the horns) was developed. Vocals for the song were recorded on October 30, 2010. It first appeared in the Sakura Gakuin album Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message, released on April 27, 2011, as part of the Jūonbu ("heavy music club") sub-unit. A limited-edition DVD single was announced on October 12, 2011, and later released as a standard digital download on October 22 and 23, 2011, available for pre-sale at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2011 held at Mt. Rainier Hall "Shibuya Pleasure Pleasure," and subsequently sold in limited quantities on ASmart, Amazon, Tower Records Online, and Tower Records Shinjuku starting October 24. The limited edition included a DVD with the "Doki Doki ☆ Morning" music video and a cut focusing on the choreography for live performances, along with a towel embossed with either the band's logo or the Juonbu Records label. A CD single was released on April 6, 2012, packaged with a T-shirt. The song was later released as a promotional single in the United Kingdom on December 13, 2015. The track features a "modern heaviness" sound with dark, atmospheric instrumentals that transition into a catchier, brighter melody, including lyrics such as "Rin rin rin! Ohayō, wake up" (Ring ring ring! Good morning, wake up). Kikuchi highlighted that the tone contrasted directly with Japanese kei-on music (light music), leading the band to form under the Jūonbu label to signify this difference. Nakamoto, whose vocals were recorded separately from Mizuno and Kikuchi, needed to speak quickly and clearly in the verses. The song peaked at number 80 on the Billboard Japan Top Independent Albums and Singles chart for the week dated November 7, 2011. Directed by Shimon Tanaka, the music video shooting was completed by October 2011; Nakamoto mentioned that Tanaka wanted to appear in it but found the choreography difficult. The abridged version of the video was released on the Toy's Factory YouTube channel on October 12, 2011, with the full version posted on the official Babymetal channel on November 8, 2012. Metal Injection ranked the music video at number nine on "The Top 15 Metal Viral Videos of the Year" on December 8, 2011. The song premiered at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2010 concert at Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No. 1 on November 28, 2010. Su-metal recalled that during the interlude of the first performance, the group pretended to fall to the ground, fearing embarrassment, but the audience's positive reaction made her feel happy and affirmed her identity as Su-metal and Babymetal. On March 4, 2012, fellow Sakura Gakuin members Marina Horiuchi, Ayaka Miyoshi, and Airi Matsui covered the song as a "Shuffle Unit" during the Sakura Gakuin concert Sakura Gakuin Hōkago Anthology at the Nihonbashi Mitsui Hall. On December 8, 2013, Hana Taguchi, Saki Ooga, and Aiko Yamaide covered it as another "Shuffle Unit" at the Sakura Gakuin 3rd Anniversary: Live at the Amuse Musical Theater. Kiba of Akiba covered the song on the joint single "Babymetal × Kiba of Akiba." Credits are adapted from the album liner notes of Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message and Babymetal.
